chunks: And from him, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Isḥāq al-ʿAlawī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hilāl, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: I enter the market of the Muslims—I mean these people who claim Islam—and I buy furs from them for trade. So I say to their owner: “Are they not properly slaughtered?” and he says: “Yes.” So is it permissible for me to sell them as being properly slaughtered?
He said: “No. However, there is no harm in your selling them and saying: ‘The one from whom I bought them stipulated that they were properly slaughtered.’”

I said: “What corrupted that?” He said: “The people of Iraq deemed carrion lawful, and they claimed that tanning the skin of carrion is its purification by slaughter. Then they were not content to lie about that except against the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.”

key_terms.الْفِرَاءَ: furs or pelts traded as merchandise
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةِ: carrion, an animal not lawfully slaughtered
key_terms.دِبَاغَ: tanning, mentioned here in the disputed claim regarding skins
key_terms.ذَكِيَّةً: properly slaughtered according to the sacred law
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ: the Messenger of Allah, to whom false claims were wrongly attributed
key_terms.سُوقَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the marketplace of Muslims, invoked here as the context of commercial dealing
key_terms.شَرَطَ: stipulated or asserted as a condition in the sale

ai.seo_question: Can a person sell furs as properly slaughtered based only on the seller’s claim in the Muslim market?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about trading in animal furs when their lawful slaughter is uncertain. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام forbids the seller from affirming as certain that the goods are properly slaughtered, but permits sale with accurate attribution to the previous seller’s claim. It also condemns false legal justifications regarding carrion skins and fabricated attribution to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.
